name: Reno Tahoe International Airport
before:
The airport for Reno and, more usefully for a holiday itinerary, for Lake Tahoe. It is named after both, and sits three miles south east of downtown Reno. For clients heading to the Tahoe ski resorts this is far closer than flying into a larger Californian airport and driving.

It is Nevada's second busiest commercial airport after Las Vegas, with three concrete runways across 1,450 acres. The elevation is worth noting at 4,415 feet, which is high enough to affect aircraft performance on a hot day.

The traffic mix is unusually broad. Across a year the airport averaged 285 movements a day, split roughly evenly between scheduled airlines and general aviation, with air taxi and military work alongside. The Nevada Air National Guard keeps its 152nd Airlift Wing just south west of the main terminal, so military aircraft are a normal sight.
after:
The airport for Reno and, more usefully for a holiday itinerary, for Lake Tahoe. It is named after both, and sits a few miles south east of downtown Reno. For clients heading to the Tahoe ski resorts this is far closer than flying into a larger Californian airport and driving.

It is Nevada's second busiest commercial airport after Las Vegas, with three concrete runways across 1,450 acres at an elevation of 4,415 feet.

The traffic mix is broad. Airlines share the field with general aviation, air taxi and military flights. The Nevada Air National Guard's 152nd Airlift Wing is based here, so military aircraft are a normal sight.

claims.note: Wikipedia does not make this point; it rests on the resort and the operator. Palisades Tahoe's own distance table puts Reno 42 miles away, Sacramento 96 and San Francisco 196, and it sends flyers to RNO; the operator puts RNO less than an hour from ski resorts and its nearest competing commercial airport 115 miles away in Sacramento. Heavenly's page gave no distances, and Sugar Bowl's site refused (405).
